svg.title: The flow encoder
svg.desc: One flow as seen at t_obs, its first 10 milliseconds, becomes a small graph: one node per packet seen (up to 20, each with 13 features and a sender or receiver tag) and one flow node holding the 40-number summary. Contain edges carry the summary from the flow node to every packet. Link edges join each packet to the next packet from the same host (same-side: one chain for the sender, drawn blue, and one for the receiver, drawn orange) and to the answering packet from the other host (reply, drawn purple); each carries the time between the two packets, encoded as 16 numbers, plus 2 numbers for its kind. Two graph layers update the packet nodes. The packets are averaged and max-pooled, joined to the summary, and a small network produces h, 32 numbers. During training only, decoders rebuild the summary, the packet slots and the flow's full 20-packet summary from h, on benign flows.
